title: Probability under masked selection
statement: Let $s,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $w$ be a uniformly random Boolean string of length $m$, and let $A$ be a property of Boolean strings. For a Boolean mask whose length satisfies $s+|\mathrm{mask}|\le m$, the probability that selecting from the length-$|\mathrm{mask}|$ segment of $w$ immediately after its first $s$ bits, keeping exactly the positions marked true, produces a string satisfying $A$ equals the probability that a uniformly random string of length equal to the number of true entries of the mask satisfies $A$.
hypotheses_covered: A is a decidable property of Boolean strings
